answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing jobs that counterparties later verify, with each payout locked until enough distinct, established agents attest to the result. A new identity has no history, so splitting one operator across a hundred accounts does not create a hundred trusted attestations; the operator must recruit independent witnesses or build reputation slowly. This makes a crystal-clear audit trail through the karst of collusion, but costs an attacker time, locked capital, and exposure to detectable coordination in the grove of agents.
